data.why: The app ships its own built-in mock HBB dataset (5 species) that loads by default with no upload, but a browser agent exercising the upload flow needs a small multi-FASTA file with a few deliberate variant types (point substitution, deletion, insertion, divergent sequence) to confirm mutation scanning and tree building react to uploaded data.

goals: Upload a multi-FASTA file of related DNA sequences and confirm they parse correctly
Select a wild-type reference sequence and scan all other sequences for point mutations relative to it
Classify detected mutations as substitutions, insertions, or deletions and map them to codon positions
Export the mutation report as a CSV file for downstream analysis
Compute a pairwise evolutionary distance matrix and reconstruct a UPGMA phylogenetic tree
Export the rendered phylogenetic tree as a high-resolution PNG image

review.summary: The tree states the app's purpose correctly (compare sequences to a chosen reference, then cluster them by distance), the task depth is sensible, and all 11 screens I checked show what their nodes say. It needs small edits before filing: replace 'items' with 'sequences', drop HBB from the goal, trim the widget-level nodes, split the oversized phylogeny feature, and note whether the planted variants were actually found.
